summary: A four-day marine science program for 18 students and 2 chaperones in Key Largo, combining classroom learning, two boat snorkels with fish surveys, and a guided kayak tour.

days.title: What Is REEF?
days.theme: Meet your REEF educators and start learning how coral reef ecosystems work.

blocks.title: Welcome to REEF
blocks.description: REEF educators welcome the group and preview the days ahead.

blocks.title: Coral Reef Ecology
blocks.description: A Florida Keys coral lesson on how reefs are built, how the organisms on them depend on each other, and how coral restoration helps reefs recover.

studentsWill: Learn what REEF is and what the four days will include.
Explain how coral reefs are built and how reef organisms depend on each other.

days.title: Become a Citizen Scientist
days.theme: Snorkel a Key Largo reef, then learn how to identify and survey the fish you saw.

blocks.title: Reef Snorkel (by boat)
blocks.description: Students board a boat to a Key Largo coral reef and snorkel to explore marine ecology firsthand: how corals, fish, and other reef organisms depend on each other. They record the fish they find using the survey method they learned. Boat times are confirmed once your dates are set.

blocks.title: Lunch (on your own)
blocks.description: Lunch is not included in this proposal. Your group can bring lunch or pick up food nearby.

blocks.title: Volunteer Fish Survey Project & Fish Identification
blocks.description: Students learn how REEF's volunteer divers and snorkelers record the fish they see, and why that data matters to scientists and reef managers. They practice identifying common Caribbean reef fish by family, body shape, color, and behavior.

studentsWill: Snorkel a Key Largo coral reef and see how its organisms depend on each other.
Learn how REEF fish survey data is collected and used.

days.title: Invasive Species and a Second Survey
days.theme: Investigate invasive lionfish up close, then return to the water for a second reef snorkel.

blocks.title: Invasive Species: Lionfish Lesson & Dissection
blocks.description: Students investigate invasive lionfish through a guided dissection, looking at anatomy and adaptations and learning why lionfish are a conservation challenge for Florida Keys reefs.

blocks.title: Lunch (on your own)
blocks.description: Lunch is not included in this proposal. Your group can bring lunch or pick up food nearby.

blocks.title: Second Reef Snorkel (by boat)
blocks.description: Students return to the reef to apply what they learned and record a second set of fish surveys. Boat times are confirmed once your dates are set.

studentsWill: Investigate invasive lionfish through a guided dissection.
Record a second set of reef fish surveys.

days.title: Protecting What We Study
days.theme: Wrap up with the species that need protection, then head home.

blocks.title: Endangered Species of the Florida Keys
blocks.description: Students learn which marine species in the Keys are threatened or endangered, such as sea turtles and staghorn and elkhorn corals, why they are at risk, and what people are doing to protect them. The session wraps up the four days.

blocks.title: Departure
blocks.description: Your group departs around noon. Lunch is not included in this proposal.

studentsWill: Identify threatened and endangered species of the Florida Keys and the actions protecting them.
Connect the week's reef surveys to conservation.
